The '''2026 Pro Bowl Games''' was the [[National Football League]] (NFL)'s [[all-star game]] for the [[2025 NFL season]]. This was the fourth and final year the event has consisted of a non-contact [[flag football]] game, and the first year it has been integrated into the [[Super Bowl]]'s festivities instead of a standalone event.<ref name="CNN-October">{{cite web|last=Martin|first=Jill|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/22/sport/football-nfl-pro-bowl-moves-to-super-bowl-week|title=The NFL's Pro Bowl is moving to Super Bowl week|website=CNN|date=October 22, 2025|access-date=November 3, 2025}}</ref> It took place in the week leading up to [[Super Bowl LX]] on Tuesday, February 3, 2026, at the [[Moscone Center]] in [[San Francisco, California]], the site of this season's [[Super Bowl Experience]].<ref name="schedule">{{cite web|title=Official lineup of Super Bowl LX events and venues revealed |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/official-lineup-of-super-bowl-lx-events-and-venues-revealed|website=NFL.com|date=November 3, 2025|access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref> The [[National Football Conference| NFC]] defended their win from the previous year's flag football game with a 66–52 win, extending their win streak to four straight, retaining their undefeated record since the format change, and allowing them to retake a 27–26 all-time lead over the AFC in Pro Bowl events.

This was the final edition of the Pro Bowl Games, as the NFL announced in August 2026 that they would be discontinued.<ref>{{cite news |title=NFL pulls the plug on the Pro Bowl |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nfl/article/nfl-pulls-the-plug-on-the-pro-bowl/ |access-date=26 August 2026 |publisher=TSN}}</ref>

==Background==
In October 2025, the NFL announced plans to integrate the Pro Bowl Games into the Super Bowl's festivities rather than continue to hold it as a standalone event. It will be designed as a more intimate, television-oriented event held inside a 4,000-seat ballroom at the [[Moscone Center]] in [[San Francisco]], the site of this season's [[Super Bowl Experience]]. The league also intends to use it as a preview for [[Flag football at the Summer Olympics|flag football's Olympics debut]] at the [[2028 Summer Olympics|2028 Games]] in [[Los Angeles]].<ref name="ESPN-October">{{cite web|title=NFL's Pro Bowl festivities moving to Tuesday of Super Bowl week |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46684395/nfl-pro-bowl-festivities-moving-tuesday-super-bowl-week|website=ESPN|date=October 22, 2025|access-date=November 3, 2025}}</ref>

==Format==
The format included a 7-on-7 flag football game held on February 3, 2026. The Skills Competition was not televised this year and did not count towards the points of the final score. Portions were shown on social media and other digital platforms. In the three prior years held that were worth points towards the final score.<ref name="nfl-announcement">{{cite web|title=2026 Pro Bowl Games Moved to Tuesday of Super Bowl LX Week in Bay Area|url=https://operations.nfl.com/updates/the-game/2026-pro-bowl-games-presented-by-verizon-moved-to-tuesday-of-super-bowl-lx-week-in-bay-area/|website=NFL.com|date=October 22, 2025|access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref>

==Rosters==
The fan voting ran from November 27, 2025, to December, with the initial rosters announced on December 23, 2025.<ref name="nfl-announcement"/> After quarterback [[Drake Maye]] and the [[2025 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] advanced to [[Super Bowl LX]], he was replaced by [[Shedeur Sanders]]; the [[2025 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] rookie was reportedly selected because a number of other AFC quarterbacks were either injured or declined to participate, but it sparked outbursts from fans due to Sanders's subpar season that included a 3–4 record, a 56.6 completion percentage, a 7-10 interception ratio, and a 68.1 [[passer rating]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Brinkerhoff|first=Nick|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2026/01/26/shedeur-sanders-pro-bowl-browns/88366394007/|title=Why is Shedeur Sanders going to the Pro Bowl? Browns QB's selection explained|website=USA Today|date=January 26, 2026|access-date=January 26, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Browns rookie QB Shedeur Sanders added to Pro Bowl Games roster as replacement|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/browns-rookie-qb-shedeur-sanders-added-to-pro-bowl-games-roster-as-replacement|website=NFL.com|access-date=January 29, 2026|language=en-US|date=January 27, 2026}}</ref>

==Broadcasting==
[[NFL on ESPN|ESPN]] will continue to produce the telecasts of the Pro Bowl Games. However, [[NFL on ABC|ABC]] will no longer simulcast the flag football game live due to the broadcast network's prior commitment to air its regular Tuesday night primetime lineup.<ref name="smw-October">{{cite web|last=Lewis|first=Jon|title=NFL announces Pro Bowl changes |url=https://www.sportsmediawatch.com/2025/10/nfl-announces-pro-bowl-changes/|website=Sports Media Watch|date=October 22, 2025|access-date=November 3, 2025}}</ref> However, ABC aired a one-hour Pro Bowl Games content special, ''Championship Chase: The Pro Bowl'' produced by [[NFL Films]] on Sunday, February 1, preceded by a special edition of ''[[NFL Live]]'' on ESPN.<ref name="nfl-announcement"/> This special was narrated by [[Method Man]] and made available on ESPN digital platforms the next day.
